sheet-2.description: The northwest part of Princeton borough, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet runs from Westcott Road at the top to Stockton Street at the bottom, and from Library Place on the west to Bayard Lane on the east edge. Hodge Road crosses the middle of the sheet from Library Place to Bayard Lane, with Boudinot Street 500 feet to the south and Cleveland Lane, which curves round the north-west block, above it. Lilac Lane and Morven run north and south between the blocks. The ground is almost entirely large residential lots with frame and brick dwellings, many with outbuildings and auto houses, some of three stories, and a few blue (stone or brick-veneer) houses. At the bottom, between Boudinot Street and Stockton Street, stand the Peacock Inn, the Princeton Junior School for Boys and the larger Princeton Inn building with its night watchman note. Streets are lettered with widths of 50 and 70 feet, and 4 inch water pipes with the year of laying (1895 to 1910) run in most streets. Hydrants, fire alarm boxes and telephone poles are marked. The left edge and the upper left corner are blank, belonging to sheets 21 and 10, and a compass rose stands on the west side. The east side of Bayard Lane is blank with the note No Exposure. The adjoining sheets are 21 to the north and west, 3 to the east, and 11 and 12 to the south.
notes: Street names read from a 1600 px overview with a check on crops; Westcott Road may be misread (the first letters are small).
Modern name of Morven is Morven Place; Boudinot is Boudinot Street; Stockton is Stockton Street.

100 ft. Northwest: Bayard Ln, Cleveland Ln, Library Pl, Boudinot, Morven, Hodge Rd, Stockton. 6 points; Bayard/Cleveland, Cleveland/Library and Boudinot/Morven excluded; scale 3 percent low, medium-low confidence.

sheet-3.description: A strip of central Princeton from the Bayard Lane and Stockton Street corner at the west to John Street at the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The top half of the sheet is the Greenholm estate, a large lot with a few big dwellings and a looped drive lettered Greenholm, with Hodge Road entering at the upper left and Green Street and Jackson Street meeting John Street on the right. Boudinot Street runs in from Bayard Lane at the left, and Hulfish Street meets John Street at the right. The lower half is the downtown block north of Nassau Street, between Bayard Lane and John Street, with Bank Street and Chambers Street running north from Nassau Street. Here the buildings change from frame dwellings along Bank Street and Chambers Street to brick commercial buildings on Nassau Street: Frank South's garage, Kurzmans garage, a large garage built in 1926 with ramps, The Princeton Bank, the Sunday school and the Second Presbyterian Church, the Mercer Engine Company No. 3 fire department house on Chambers Street, a boarding house, contractors' workshop, hay, feed and grain store, a photographer and a kitchen. A house lettered as the Dorothea's House stands at the top right. Water pipes laid in 1883 to 1903 run in the streets. A compass rose is on the right. Adjoining sheets are 2 and 5 to the north, 12 and 13 to the south and 6 to the east.
notes: Bank Street is drawn ending short of Chambers Street; in OpenStreetMap it joins Chambers Street, so that junction was left out.
Chambers Street and John Street do not meet where OpenStreetMap places them (Paul Robeson Place); that junction was left out.
Names read from a 1600 px overview; the house name at the top right is uncertain.
50 ft. Bayard Ln, Bank, Chambers, Nassau, John, Greenholm. Bank/Chambers and Chambers/John excluded (merged/realigned nodes, as 1911).

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the northwest part of Princeton borough at 50 feet to an inch, a district of frame dwellings between John Street on the west and Witherspoon Street on the east. The map runs from the trolley right of way along the top, past Birch Avenue and Leigh Avenue, down to Clay Street and Lytle Street at the bottom. The streets are laid out in narrow blocks of closely spaced two-storey frame dwellings, many with rear outbuildings, with the lot lines drawn throughout. A coal bin shed and an ice house stand beside the trolley right of way at the top, with a contractor's storehouse, an old box yard, a wood working shop and a Church of God in Christ in the blocks below it. A line of rowhouse-type frame dwellings runs along the west side of John Street, and a belt of lots to the west is marked as the continuation of sheets 14, 15, 16 and 18. The Sanitary Ice Company plant, a tile building with watchman, heat, steam, lights and electricity noted, stands near Witherspoon Street in the lower right block. A dash-dot borough line crosses the sheet near the middle, running through the blocks between Leigh and Clay streets. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn along several streets with their dates. A compass rose with a north arrow appears at the left, and the north arrow points toward the upper left of the sheet. Adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins: 14, 15, 16 and 18 to the west, 17 above, 5 below.
notes: Placed from John Street and Witherspoon Street junctions only; Birch Avenue and the Leigh Avenue / Witherspoon Street junction were left out because their modern lines do not fit the drawn ones (4 to 11 m residuals). Low confidence.
Fitted scale about 7.5 px/ft against about 8.1 expected for 50 feet to an inch; Witherspoon Street junction spacing is about 15 percent shorter on the sheet than today.
50 ft. Birch Av to Lytle, John to Witherspoon. Birch Avenue junctions (8 to 11 m) and Leigh/Witherspoon (11 m) left out as displaced; low confidence.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the Witherspoon Street district of Princeton borough at 50 feet to an inch, the block between John Street on the west and Witherspoon Street on the east, from Lytle Street at the top to Green Street at the bottom. Mac Lean Street and Quarry Street cross it between them, and Witherspoon Lane enters at the top right. The district is largely frame dwellings on narrow lots, with a few larger buildings: the B.P.O.E. club house, an apartment building, Douglas Hall, the Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, an Odd Fellows Hall, the Witherspoon Public School (Colored), and the Witherspoon Presbyterian Church with its parish house. The centre of the sheet holds the Princeton University polo stables and an auto repair shop, with Acton Court running south from the stables. A bakery stands at the upper right, and an iron water tank on an iron tower is drawn at the left edge. A strip west of John Street is drawn with houses and outbuildings along the street, with a lane marked not named. Along the right edge a cemetery entrance and cemetery are lettered, with a narrow burial ground drawn beside Witherspoon Street. Four and six inch water pipes are dated along the streets. A compass rose appears at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets are 4 above, 6 below, 3 to the lower left and 18 to the upper right.
notes: Maclean Street in OpenStreetMap is lettered Mac Lean on the sheet.
50 ft. John to Witherspoon, Lytle to Green; Maclean, Quarry.

sheet-6-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 6 is the main map, east of the heavy vertical line that separates it from the Alexander Street strip, and covers the centre of Princeton borough at 50 feet to an inch. It runs from Green Street at the top, past Jackson Street and Hulfish Street, down to Nassau Street at the bottom, between John Street on the west and Witherspoon Street on the east, with Baker Street and Nassau Place inside the blocks. The upper blocks hold frame dwellings and, among them, the Bright Hope Baptist Church (Colored), an auto repair shop, and the Y.M.C.H. building. The block between Jackson and Hulfish streets holds the Borough of Princeton buildings, a storehouse and a line of small dwellings. South of Hulfish Street the blocks are denser: a large garage with repair and machine shops stands in the middle of the block beside Nassau Place, and the Fire Department with its hose and chemical engine company, the Witherspoon Hotel, an ice cream factory, a bakery, pool rooms and stores line Witherspoon Street. The Nassau Street frontage along the bottom is built solid with brick stores, the Nassau Inn with its dining room and kitchen, a tailor shop and the First National Bank. A livery stable and carriage sheds stand west of Nassau Place. A compass rose with a north arrow appears at the right and the north arrow points toward the top of the page. Sheets 5 above, 3 at left, 7 at right and 13 below adjoin.
notes: Only the Witherspoon Street junctions and John Street / Green Street are used; the junctions at Jackson Street (now Paul Robeson Place), Palmer Square and Hulfish Street do not fit the drawn lines because the modern streets were realigned. Four of the five control points are hand-picked from the street width and pipes, one with rough readings. Low confidence.
Jackson Street is Paul Robeson Place in OpenStreetMap; the old John Street / Jackson Street corner lies under the modern Chambers Street / John Street / Paul Robeson Place node, which did not match.
Baker Street is probably the modern Chambers Street; not verified.

50 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Green to Nassau, John to Witherspoon; 5 hand-picked points nearly along Witherspoon; Jackson = Paul Robeson Pl, Palmer Square and Chambers junctions realigned, left out), 2 left strip along Alexander St and the railroad (lumber, coal, building materials; unplaced).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: left strip: Alexander Street along the railroad, lumber, coal and building-material yards (no street junction; needs step 6b: a feature shared with sheet 17 part 2 (none found)).

sheet-7.description: This sheet, turned so that Nassau Street runs up the right-hand side and Witherspoon Street along the foot, covers the blocks of central Princeton west of Nassau Street and north of Witherspoon Street. The north-south streets are Wiggins Street at the left, Spring Street and Park Place in the middle, and Lincoln Court and Nassau Street on the right; the cross streets are Madison Street at the top, Van Deventer Avenue, North Tulane Street and South Tulane Street. The upper half, between Madison Street and Van Deventer Avenue, is a district of detached frame dwellings on narrow lots, with the Princeton M. E. Church and a smaller church at Park Place. Along Nassau Street the drawing changes to a continuous row of brick commercial buildings: shops, a moving picture house, the post office at the corner of Witherspoon Street and a public library near Van Deventer Avenue. The lower left is occupied by the Public Service Gas and Electric Company yard, with a gas holder, transformer yard and electric works, labelled no manufacturing. Garages and a dormitory stand between Spring Street and Lincoln Court. The Princeton University Library map division stamp and the date October 1927 appear on the sheet, and its neighbours are numbered at the edges: 8 above, 6 below, 13 and 14 to the right and 19 to the left. A scale of feet is printed at the foot.
notes: Read on 1600 px overviews, not full-resolution crops: names fainter than the main labels (Robert Street and Greenview Avenue at the left edge, Jackson Street at the foot) are uncertain or left out.
Van Deventer Avenue is Vandeventer Avenue in OpenStreetMap; North and South Tulane Street are the modern names.
Paul Robeson Place at Witherspoon Street is realigned; its modern junction is not used as control.
50 ft, turned (north to the left). Madison to Witherspoon, Wiggins to Nassau; Spring, Tulane, Vandeventer.

sheet-8.description: This sheet, turned like its neighbours so that Nassau Street runs up the right-hand side, shows the blocks between Chestnut Street at the top and Madison Street at the foot, west of Nassau Street. Chestnut Street and Moran Avenue are lined on their north side with detached frame dwellings, with a church group at the Nassau Street end. The centre of the sheet is an open, unbuilt tract crossed by faint property lines and labelled cemetery, with a compass rose, bounded by Spruce Street on the left. On Nassau Street stand St. Paul's R. C. Church with its parish hall, rectory, St. Paul's School and a convent. Below Moore Street the drawing is again closely built: dwellings along Wiggins Street, Willow Street and Park Place, the University Laundry Company works between Moore Street and Branch Avenue, and a planing mill at Branch Avenue. A row of dwellings lines Madison Street along the foot. The sheet is dated October 1927 and carries the Princeton University Library map division stamp; the adjoining sheets are numbered 9 above, 7 below, 19 to the left and 15 and 14 to the right.
notes: Read on 1600 px overviews, not full-resolution crops; faint street labels on the left edge and at the right (Hamilton and Charlton) were left out.
Junctions of Moore Street and of Moran Avenue with Spruce Street are not used as control.
50 ft, turned. Chestnut to Madison, Wiggins to Nassau, Moran Av, Moore; cemetery tract blank.

sheet-9.description: Residential blocks on the north side of Nassau Street in the eastern part of Princeton borough, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The sheet runs from Chestnut Street on the west to Linden Lane on the east, and from the lots on the north side of Spruce Street, with the corner of Hamilton Avenue at the top left, down to Nassau Street along the bottom edge. Pine Street and Maple Street run north from Nassau Street between them, and Murray Place meets Nassau Street at the lower right, where the sheet stops. Almost all of the buildings are frame dwellings, most of two or two and a half stories, set in long narrow lots with outbuildings and auto houses behind. Two public garages stand out: a concrete-block garage for 30 cars at Spruce and Pine Streets, and a larger garage for 50 cars with heat by steam behind the Nassau Street frontage between Chestnut and Pine Streets, next to a wood yard with a wood shed and wood pile. Princeton Engine Company No. 1, the fire department house, is on the east side of Chestnut Street. The Nassau Street frontage, numbered 238 to 276, is a row of dwellings and small stores. Water pipes with their sizes and dates of laying are drawn in every street, and hydrants are marked. Street widths of 40 to 60 feet are lettered at the ends of the blocks. A compass rose stands at the right edge beside Linden Lane, whose east side is left blank for sheet 19. The adjoining sheets are 8 to the west, 15 and 16 to the south and 19 to the east.
notes: Princeton Engine Co. No. 1 (fire department) on Chestnut Street.
A 50-car public garage stands behind the Nassau Street frontage between Chestnut and Pine.
50 ft. Chestnut, Spruce, Pine, Maple, Linden Lane, Nassau, Murray Pl, Hamilton Av corner. Pilot sheet: ink_below_paper 100 (138 finds nothing), min_width_ratio 0.6; 9 points, RMSE 1.4 m.

sheet-10-1.description: The west edge of Princeton, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the sheet made up of two photographs joined at a vertical seam. The part covers the right side of the sheet, east of the heavy line that separates the Prospect Avenue strip (part 2). Stockton Street crosses the top, with Elm Road entering at the upper left and a greenhouse range (lettered Green Hos.) at the top right. Lovers Lane runs down the left side of the part, meeting Mercer Street, which crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right at a shallow angle. Springdale Road (College Road) runs down the right side. Battle Road runs along the lower part from the borough line towards Springdale Road, with a row of frame houses along it, and Oldens Lane and Hazlet Road are lettered at the bottom edge. The rest of the ground is lawns and open land belonging to large estates, lots numbered 43, 501 and 502, with scattered frame dwellings and a few blue stone buildings; there is little drawn building area. The borough line crosses the lower part in a dot and dash line. A compass rose stands in the open ground at the upper right. Water pipes of 1883 and 1910 run in Mercer Street, Stockton Street and Springdale Road. Adjoining sheets are 11 to the east, 20 to the south and west, and 16 and 15 on the left.
notes: Oldens Lane is Olden Lane today; Hazlet Road is Haslet Avenue today.
Springdale Road is lettered '(College Rd.)'; the Battle Road and Olden Lane junction was left out as it does not match the modern node.
The Lovers Lane, Mercer Street and Olden Lane junction was not detected.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main right of the heavy line (Lovers Ln, Mercer, Battle Rd, Stockton; Battle/Olden left out), 2 Prospect Av strip left of the line (helmert on two points). Scan is two photographs joined near full-res x 4640.

sheet-10-2.description: A strip along the west side of Prospect Avenue at the east edge of the sheet's left side, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 70 degrees, with north pointing to the upper left. It is separated from the main part of the sheet by a heavy line. Prospect Avenue runs up the left edge from Washington Road at the bottom, and Olden Street joins it from the west at about the middle. Along the avenue stand the Princeton University eating clubs on lots numbered 70 to 86: Campus Club, Tower Club, Terrace Club, Cannon Club, Quadrangle Club, Ivy Club, Cottage Club, Cap and Gown Club, Cloister Inn Club, Charter Club and Key and Seal Club. They are brick and stone buildings drawn in pink and blue, with servants' quarters behind. East of the clubs the ground is lettered as the property of Princeton University, with a field house at the centre and Roma Road, lettered as arbitrary, running down beside the heavy line. Washington Road crosses the bottom of the strip with a 4 inch water pipe and a fire alarm box at the corner. A north arrow stands at the top. The adjoining sheets are 15 and 16 to the left and 13 to the south.
notes: Placed from two junctions: Olden Street / Prospect Avenue (detected) and Prospect Avenue / Washington Road (hand-picked); helmert.
The strip is the same Prospect Avenue strip drawn as part of sheet 10 in the 1911 edition.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main right of the heavy line (Lovers Ln, Mercer, Battle Rd, Stockton; Battle/Olden left out), 2 Prospect Av strip left of the line (helmert on two points). Scan is two photographs joined near full-res x 4640.

sheet-11.description: The Princeton Theological Seminary and the university's Graduate College area west of the borough centre, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Stockton Street runs across the top and Mercer Street crosses the sheet from the lower left to the upper right, with Edgehill, Library Place and Hibben Road running north from it. Between Stockton Street and Mercer Street are the Hun School for boys (a preparatory school), the Seminary Library, the Thompson Hall branch of the public library with Rose Cottage, and rows of small frame houses along Edgehill and Library Place. South of Mercer Street the Theological Seminary of the Presbyterian Church lettered across the grounds includes Alexander Hall, Miller Chapel, Hodge Hall, Brown Hall, Stuart Hall and a gymnasium, and the ground continues to the Golf Links and the Princeton Graduate College with Thompson College, Procter Hall and Wyman Hall, built round courts in blue. Stockton Place curves around the links to Alexander Street, which runs down the right edge, and University Place is lettered at the lower right near the Princeton Inn. Springdale Road, also lettered College Road, runs down the left edge. The borough line crosses near the bottom. A compass rose stands at the centre. Adjoining sheets are 2 to the north, 12 and 17 to the east, 10 to the west.
notes: Stockton Place is College Road today; Library Place and Mercer Street do not meet where OpenStreetMap places the junction, and Edgehill Street / Mercer Street is displaced about 5 m; both junctions were left out.
Alexander Street / College Road junction was excluded (about 5 m residual).
100 ft. Mercer, Stockton, Alexander, College Rd, seminary grounds. Library/Mercer, Alexander/College Road and Edgehill/Mercer left out (5 m).

sheet-12.description: The block around Mercer Street and Nassau Street at the west end of the university campus in central Princeton, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Stockton Street runs across the top left, with Trinity Church and its parish house, a rectory and Trinity Club on its south side. Mercer Street runs diagonally from the lower left to the Nassau Street corner at the top right, with the Nassau Club and its stable, houses and stores along it. Alexander Street runs from the Mercer Street side down to Dickinson Street at the bottom, with a street of frame houses and, on its east side, a row of ten identical frame dwellings on Edward Place. University Place runs down the right edge to Dickinson Street. The east side of the sheet holds large frame and brick houses including a Hall apartment building, Kolbe House and Craig House, a 14-car garage, and a block of apartments. Water pipes from 1883 and 1910 run in Mercer Street and Nassau Street. Most buildings are frame, two to three stories, with a few brick and stone buildings in pink and blue. A compass rose stands at the lower left. Adjoining sheets are 2 and 3 to the north, 11 to the west, 13 to the east and 17 to the south.
notes: Edward Pl. is Edwards Place in OpenStreetMap.
The Mercer Street and Nassau Street junction (an acute angle) was not detected; control rests on four points.
50 ft. Stockton, Mercer, Alexander, Edwards Pl, University Pl, Dickinson, Nassau; 4 points.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 13 shows the central campus of Princeton University at 100 feet to an inch, the only sheet of the atlas besides sheet 21 and a few others drawn at that scale. The map is bounded on the north by Nassau Street, on the west by University Place and on the east by Washington Road, with Prospect Avenue entering from the east and Dickinson Street and Edward Place from the west. Nearly all of the ground is occupied by university buildings coloured blue for brick and pink or tan for other fireproof construction. Along Nassau Street stand Madison, Sage, Hamilton and Holder halls, the First Presbyterian Church, Alexander Hall, Nassau Hall (built 1756), Stanhope Hall, the Library, and the School of Science. Blair Hall, West College, Witherspoon Hall, Little Hall, Clio and Whig halls, Dodds Hall, the Art Museum, McCormick Hall and the University Chapel fill the middle. Along University Place are Lockhart Hall, Walter Foulke Hall, Howard Henry Hall, Laughlin Hall and Pyne Hall, and the gymnasium with its swimming tank and the University Power Company plant lie to the south. Brown Hall, Cuyler Hall, Patton Hall, the Palmer Physical Laboratory, McCosh Infirmary, Guyot Hall and McCosh Hall stand toward the east and south. A note states the watchmen, clocks and power arrangements. A boxed inset at the bottom, with its own north arrow, shows the Hobart Baker Memorial Rink and the University Power and Heat Plant. A railroad spur crosses the lower left, and a borough line runs across the bottom. The sheet adjoins sheets 3, 6 and 7 above, 12 and 17 at left, and 14 and 10 at right.
notes: The Hobart Baker Memorial Rink inset at the bottom (boxed, north arrow turned toward the upper right) is a separate part and was not placed (no street junction).

Control is two detected junctions (Washington Road / William Street, Dickinson Street / University Place) and four hand-picked pipe crossings at street centres; the leave-one-out error is about 6 m. Low to medium confidence.
Vandeventer Avenue is lettered Van Deventer Av. on the sheet.
100 ft. Two parts: 1 university campus (2 detected, 4 hand-picked water-pipe crossings), 2 boxed inset of Hobart Baker Memorial Rink and the power and heat plant (unplaced).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: boxed inset: Hobart Baker Memorial Rink and University power and heat plant (no street junction; needs parcel corners or building corners).

sheet-14.description: This sheet covers the University campus area south of Nassau Street, between Washington Road on the left and Charlton Street on the right, and extends south to Prospect Avenue. The top row of blocks, north of William Street, has frame dwellings and the Model Public School and Princeton Grammar School with its gymnasium and annex, the School of Chemistry with its annex at the corner of Nassau Street and Washington Road, and a telephone building near Charlton Street. Below William Street the drawing is dominated by large University buildings: the School of Engineering, the Chemical Laboratory with an auditorium, a maintenance shop, and on the right the Princeton University Press. At the foot, along Prospect Avenue, are the Observatory, the Washington Inn and the Colonial Club, with scattered dwellings. Large parts of the sheet are open ground. A compass rose sits at lower left and a scale of feet at the foot. The sheet is dated October 1927 and carries the Princeton University Library map division stamp; the adjoining sheets are 7 and 8 above, 13 to the left, 15 to the right and 10 below.
notes: Read on 1600 px overviews, not full-resolution crops; a street lettered along the School of Engineering (probably Van Deventer Avenue) was not legible and is left out.
50 ft. Nassau to Prospect Av, Washington Rd to Charlton; university buildings; 5 points.

sheet-15.description: This sheet shows the eastern end of the University district between Charlton Street on the left and the edge of the town's built area on the right, from Nassau Street at the top to Prospect Avenue at the foot. A single strip of closely set dwellings, garages and a few clubs lies along Charlton Street, between Nassau Street and William Street, with a garage and a church at the left edge. Olden Street runs south from William Street. The greater part of the sheet is open land of the University: the Princeton University Athletic Field with bleachers and a field house, Freshman's Field and a compass rose. South of William Street, on Prospect Avenue and the lanes behind it, stand the Tiger Inn Club, the Elm Club house, the Cannon Club house and the First Church of Christ Scientist. A large garage and a field house stand at the right. The sheet is dated October 1927 and carries the Princeton University Library map division stamp; adjoining sheets are 8 to the upper left, 9 above, 16 to the right, 14 to the left and 10 below.
notes: Read on 1600 px overviews, not full-resolution crops; some club names (Colonial, Cap and Gown) were too small to read and are left out of the description.
50 ft. Charlton to the athletic field, Nassau to Prospect Av; 5 points.

sheet-16-1.description: This is the main part of a sheet at 100 feet to an inch, covering the western edge of the town where Nassau Street, Princeton Avenue, Murray Place and Fitz Randolph Road leave the closely built area. Nassau Street crosses the top. Murray Place, Princeton Avenue and Harrison Street run south from it, crossed by Aiken Avenue, Patton Avenue and Prospect Avenue, with Broadmead and The Western Way below. Most of the area is detached dwellings on large lots; Prospect Apartments stands on Prospect Avenue near Murray Place, a mill and a group of buildings stand at the left edge, and a compass rose and a scale of 100 ft to one inch are printed. A railroad line crosses the lower part of the sheet. Heavy lines mark off a block at the right (Western Way and Harrison Street), a block at the lower right (Nassau Street, Markham Road, Wilton) and a block at the lower left (the road to Princeton and a grist mill beside the Delaware and Raritan Canal), each drawn separately.
notes: Read on 1600 px overviews, not full-resolution crops; the descriptions of buildings are approximate.
Sergeant Avenue and Pelham Avenue are Sergeant Street and Pelham Street in OpenStreetMap.
Fitz Randolph Road and most Harrison Street junctions are realigned and are not used as control.

100 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines: 1 main (Nassau to Western Way, Murray Pl to Harrison; detector ink 30), 2 right block (Western Way / Harrison, unplaced), 3 lower right (Nassau, Markham, Wilton, Sergeant), 4 lower left (road to Princeton, grist mill, canal; unplaced).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: right block: Western Way and Harrison Street houses (no checked junction (Harrison junctions realigned); needs hand-picked control from sheet 19 or part 1).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower left: road to Princeton, grist mill, Delaware and Raritan Canal (no street junction; needs hand-picked points).

sheet-16-3.description: This part of the sheet is a block drawn separately at the lower right, divided from the main map by a heavy line, showing Nassau Street along the top and the streets running south from it, Markham Road and Wilton, with Sergeant Avenue and Pelham Avenue crossing them. The blocks hold detached frame dwellings and a few outbuildings, with larger open lots at the top, one labelled with the owner's name, Lloyd Grover. A four inch water pipe is drawn in Markham Road and in Wilton. A north arrow stands at the upper right and the drawing is at 100 ft to an inch. Lot numbers 162 to 165 are printed on the blocks. The lots south of Sergeant Avenue are small and regular, with a dwelling and a shed on each, and those north of it are large.
notes: Read on a full-resolution crop for the upper part (Nassau, Sergeant Av., Wilton, Markham) and the overview for the rest.
Markham is printed without a visible suffix on the crop read; it is Markham Road today. Sergeant Avenue and Pelham Avenue are Sergeant Street and Pelham Street today.

100 ft. Four parts divided by heavy lines: 1 main (Nassau to Western Way, Murray Pl to Harrison; detector ink 30), 2 right block (Western Way / Harrison, unplaced), 3 lower right (Nassau, Markham, Wilton, Sergeant), 4 lower left (road to Princeton, grist mill, canal; unplaced).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: right block: Western Way and Harrison Street houses (no checked junction (Harrison junctions realigned); needs hand-picked control from sheet 19 or part 1).
Not georeferenced on this sheet: lower left: road to Princeton, grist mill, Delaware and Raritan Canal (no street junction; needs hand-picked points).

sheet-17-1.description: The main part of sheet 17, at 50 feet to an inch: Alexander Street on the south side of the university, from Dickinson Street at the top down past College Road and the lower end of University Place to the borough line near the bottom edge. Dickinson Street and University Place frame the top right, where three-story frame dwellings line Dickinson Street and the Trenton Traction Company waiting room stands near University Place. Below them a long row of brick faculty houses, numbered 1 to 13, runs diagonally across the block north of College Road. Stockton Place leaves Alexander Street to the west opposite College Road. The east side of Alexander Street south of College Road is lined with frame dwellings numbered 70 to 118, interrupted by University Place, which is drawn here 100 feet wide; on its south corner stands a concrete-block garage for 40 cars with a steel truss roof. The west side of Alexander Street is mostly open, with a few houses and an insurance office in block 155; a pond is drawn in blue at the lower left corner, beside the scale of feet. A compass rose stands at the upper left. The rest of Alexander Street, with the railroad and the coal and lumber yards beside it, is drawn in two strips to the right of the heavy lines (parts 2 and 3).
notes: Stockton Place west of Alexander Street is today part of College Road.
The lower stretch of University Place, 100 ft wide to Alexander Street, no longer exists as drawn.
Placed from three junctions only (Alexander / Dickinson, Dickinson / University Place, Alexander / College Road), so the fit has no redundancy.

50 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines, all along Alexander St: part 1 main (Dickinson, University Pl, College Rd, Stockton Pl, faculty houses; 3 junctions), part 2 right strip (Alexander nos. 180-226, Grover & Gulick lumber, coal bins, bottling works, Princeton Branch RR; no junction), part 3 middle strip (Alexander nos. 120-170, Princeton Inn servants quarters; placed from a point carried from part 1 at the borough line).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: right strip: Alexander Street nos. 180-226, Grover & Gulick lumber yard, coal bins, B. S. Featherstone bottling works, Princeton Branch railroad (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet 6 (adjoins at the bottom) or from part 3).

sheet-17-3.description: A narrow strip in the middle of sheet 17, between heavy lines, at 50 feet to an inch: the continuation of Alexander Street south of the borough line, with the house numbers 120 to 170 on its east side, drawn beside the main map rather than in its true place south of it. The east side of the street is lined with frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories on narrow lots, with a few auto houses and sheds behind. On the west side stand the servants' quarters of the Princeton Inn, a brick garage for 60 cars with a concrete floor and wooden roof, and an 8,000-gallon water tank on a tower. Near the bottom of the strip is the greenhouse and store of Theo. Knoche, florist. Tracks of the Princeton branch railroad run down the east edge of the strip. A north arrow is drawn beside the railroad. The street continues in the right-hand strip of the sheet (part 2) with the coal and lumber yards.
notes: Placed from one point carried from part 1 (the borough line at the east edge of Alexander Street) with the scale and rotation of part 1; low confidence.
Servants' quarters of the Princeton Inn; Theo. Knoche, florist.

50 ft. Three parts divided by heavy lines, all along Alexander St: part 1 main (Dickinson, University Pl, College Rd, Stockton Pl, faculty houses; 3 junctions), part 2 right strip (Alexander nos. 180-226, Grover & Gulick lumber, coal bins, bottling works, Princeton Branch RR; no junction), part 3 middle strip (Alexander nos. 120-170, Princeton Inn servants quarters; placed from a point carried from part 1 at the borough line).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: right strip: Alexander Street nos. 180-226, Grover & Gulick lumber yard, coal bins, B. S. Featherstone bottling works, Princeton Branch railroad (no street junction; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet 6 (adjoins at the bottom) or from part 3).

sheet-18-1.description: The top and largest part of sheet 18, at 50 feet to an inch: the residential blocks on Birch Avenue and Leigh Avenue in the north of Princeton, between Bayard Lane on the west and the edge of the sheet beyond Race Street on the east. The trolley right of way crosses the top of the sheet above an almost empty block, and Birch Avenue below it has a long row of narrow lots on its south side, most of them still vacant; only the corner of Race Street is built up with two-story frame dwellings. Between Birch and Leigh Avenues, west of Race Street, the block holds a scattering of frame houses, one large square building marked with a cross and a few auto houses. The north side of Leigh Avenue from Bayard Lane eastward, by contrast, is lined with closely spaced frame dwellings numbered 70 to 120, several drawn from plans, one brick-veneered double house and a row of four attached dwellings, with an ice house, tool house and coop behind them. The borough line runs along Leigh Avenue. A compass rose stands below the Leigh Avenue lots. The east edge adjoins sheet 4; the lower part of the page holds two separately drawn parts (the hospital on Franklin Avenue and the preparatory school on Snowden Lane), divided from this part by heavy lines.
notes: The trolley right of way along the top is the line of the former New Jersey and Pennsylvania Traction trolley road (Johnson Trolley Line trail today).
Race on the sheet is today's Race Street.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 top (Bayard Ln, Birch Av, Leigh Av, Race; 4 junctions), 2 lower left (Franklin Av / Witherspoon, Princeton Hospital 1927; north points left; anchored), 3 lower right (Snowden Ln / Nassau, Princeton Preparatory School; anchored).

sheet-18-2.description: A separately drawn part at the lower left of sheet 18, at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left: the ground north of Witherspoon Street at Franklin Avenue, with Witherspoon Lane at its east edge. It is fenced off from the Birch and Leigh Avenue map above by a heavy line. The dominant building is the new Princeton Hospital, an H-shaped fireproof building of concrete with exposed steel girders and roof trusses, built in 1927, with a power house of 1927 behind it to the west, both drawn partly from plans. South of it on Witherspoon Street stands the frame Princeton Temporary Hospital. The borough line runs through the hospital grounds. East of Franklin Avenue, toward Witherspoon Lane, are frame dwellings and a row of attached houses numbered 10 to 34 on the lane, a brick-veneered and frame building at block 139, and a group of dwellings at 215 to 223 Witherspoon Street. Witherspoon Street runs along the bottom edge with its water pipe of 1895; the street is shown with its width of 50 feet, as is Franklin Avenue, and Witherspoon Lane is lettered 15 feet wide.
notes: Princeton Hospital, built 1927, fireproof; Princeton Temporary Hospital on Witherspoon Street.
North points to the left on this part.

Witherspoon Lane is drawn 15 ft wide; the detector put its junction with Witherspoon Street on the heavy dividing line, so it is excluded and the part is anchored on Franklin Avenue / Witherspoon Street.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 top (Bayard Ln, Birch Av, Leigh Av, Race; 4 junctions), 2 lower left (Franklin Av / Witherspoon, Princeton Hospital 1927; north points left; anchored), 3 lower right (Snowden Ln / Nassau, Princeton Preparatory School; anchored).

sheet-18-3.description: A separately drawn part at the lower right of sheet 18, at 50 feet to an inch, showing the grounds of the Princeton Preparatory School (J. B. Fine, proprietor, 100 students) on the east side of Snowden Lane at Nassau Street, at the eastern edge of the town. The part is divided from the rest of the sheet by heavy lines and has its own north arrow. The school group in the middle of the grounds is a frame building of dormitories and a kitchen with a coal vault, with a separate frame school building and a second dormitory to the north and a large gymnasium with a steel truss roof set at an angle near the east edge. The school's note records no watchman, a water supply from two open wells, 100 feet of hose and fire extinguishers. Snowden Lane, 40 feet wide, runs along the west side with the borough line beside it, and Nassau Street along the bottom, with a 6-inch water pipe of 1912. One small frame dwelling stands south of Nassau Street. The rest of the ground is open; the margins are marked no exposure. The scale of feet is printed in Nassau Street.
notes: Princeton Preparatory School, J. B. Fine, proprietor.

50 ft. Three parts: 1 top (Bayard Ln, Birch Av, Leigh Av, Race; 4 junctions), 2 lower left (Franklin Av / Witherspoon, Princeton Hospital 1927; north points left; anchored), 3 lower right (Snowden Ln / Nassau, Princeton Preparatory School; anchored).

sheet-19-1.description: The main and largest part of sheet 19, at 100 feet to an inch: the residential district north of Spruce Street on the east side of Princeton, from Franklin Avenue along the top down to Wiggins Street and Spruce Street along the bottom, and from the Princeton Cemetery on the west to Chestnut Street on the east. Jefferson Road and Moore Street run down the middle of the part, with long rows of narrow lots and frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories; Hawthorne Avenue crosses east of Moore Street, and Hamilton Avenue runs diagonally from the corner of Moore and Wiggins Streets toward Chestnut Street, where its blocks are mostly laid out but still empty. In the lower left, between the cemetery and Jefferson Road, Greenview Avenue, Humbert Street and Humbert Lane hold a dense group of small dwellings with a bakery, a tin shop and a few stores; the cemetery itself is left blank. The street continuing north from Chestnut Street to Hawthorne Avenue is drawn 70 feet wide. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths are shown throughout, and the scale bar is printed in Wiggins Street. A strip at the top of the part, above Franklin Avenue, shows the south ends of the lots on its north side; the blocks beyond are drawn in an inset to the right (part 3). The part is cut off from the Nassau Street area above (part 2) by a heavy line. A compass rose stands at the right edge.
notes: Humbert Street, Humbert Lane and Greenview Avenue junctions sit about 7 m from a fit to the rest of the part and were left out; those streets appear to have been realigned since.
The street north of Chestnut Street to Hawthorne Avenue is Walnut Lane today.
The Franklin Avenue junctions are hand-picked: the detector locked onto the strip of lot ends between Franklin Avenue and the dividing line.

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main lower (Franklin Av to Spruce, Jefferson Rd, Moore, Hawthorne, Hamilton, Wiggins, Chestnut; Humbert St, Humbert Lane, Greenview Av left out as displaced), 2 top (Nassau from Linden Ln to Wilton St, Spruce, Evelyn Pl, Ewing = N Harrison St, stone quarries), 3 inset right (north side of Franklin Av, Jefferson Rd to Moore; helmert on two points).

sheet-19-2.description: The upper part of sheet 19, at 100 feet to an inch, separated from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line: the north side of Nassau Street at the east end of Princeton, from Linden Lane on the west to beyond Wilton Street on the east, with Spruce Street along the top. Linden Lane and the narrow Spruce Lane hold a row of small frame dwellings and a plumbing and tin shop. Most of the interior is open ground: a large stone quarry occupies the block between Spruce Street and the Nassau Street lots, and a second stone quarry lies east of Ewing, the road running north from Nassau Street. Evelyn Place, a short street ending in a circle, has a few dwellings. The Nassau Street frontage, numbered 280 to 404, is lined with dwellings, two auto repair shops, one of concrete block, gasoline tanks and a fireproof reinforced-concrete auto house at the east end. Below Nassau Street, Princeton Avenue, Markham Street and Wilton Street are lettered at the edge of the part, where the street ends are shown only as stubs above the dividing line. A north arrow stands in the open ground east of Ewing.
notes: Ewing on the sheet is today's North Harrison Street; Markham Street is Markham Road.
Two stone quarries are drawn north of Nassau Street.

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main lower (Franklin Av to Spruce, Jefferson Rd, Moore, Hawthorne, Hamilton, Wiggins, Chestnut; Humbert St, Humbert Lane, Greenview Av left out as displaced), 2 top (Nassau from Linden Ln to Wilton St, Spruce, Evelyn Pl, Ewing = N Harrison St, stone quarries), 3 inset right (north side of Franklin Av, Jefferson Rd to Moore; helmert on two points).

sheet-19-3.description: A small inset at the right of sheet 19, outlined by heavy lines and drawn at 100 feet to an inch: the blocks on the north side of Franklin Avenue between Jefferson Road and Moore Street and east of Moore Street, numbered 129, 130 and 132, placed beside the main map rather than in their true position north of it. The lots are long and narrow, facing Jefferson Road and Moore Street, and carry frame dwellings of two stories, a few with auto houses; one brick-veneered dwelling stands on Jefferson Road and several lots are empty. The borough line crosses the inset from west to east. Franklin Avenue is drawn only as its north edge along the bottom of the inset, with water pipes in Jefferson Road and Moore Street and fire alarm boxes at the corners. The margins are marked no exposure.
notes: Placed from two points on Franklin Avenue (Jefferson Road, Moore Street); the Moore Street corner is hand-picked half the street width below the drawn north edge.

100 ft. Three parts: 1 main lower (Franklin Av to Spruce, Jefferson Rd, Moore, Hawthorne, Hamilton, Wiggins, Chestnut; Humbert St, Humbert Lane, Greenview Av left out as displaced), 2 top (Nassau from Linden Ln to Wilton St, Spruce, Evelyn Pl, Ewing = N Harrison St, stone quarries), 3 inset right (north side of Franklin Av, Jefferson Rd to Moore; helmert on two points).

sheet-20-1.description: Outlying estates and farmland on the southwest side of Princeton, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, so the sheet is turned well away from the town sheets. Stockton Street runs down the left half of the sheet from Elm Road at the top, past the Edgerstoune estate subdivision, to the Stony Brook bridge near the bottom, where the road called Stony Brook leaves it to the east. Mercer Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the junction of Lovers Lane and Oldens Lane to the Stony Brook road at the bottom right. Oldens Lane runs along the top right, with Battle Road, Hazlet Road and Ober Road meeting it; the borough line follows Lovers Lane. Most of the sheet is open ground with a few large houses drawn individually: Constitution Hill and the Junius S. Morgan house at the upper left, Drumthwacket, the Moses Taylor Pyne estate along Mercer Street with its greenhouses, Peep O'Day, Maple Hill Farm of Walter G. Olden, Mercer Manor and Henry B. Owsley's house. The Edgerstoune tract is laid out as a loop of new roads, two of them lettered "not named", around a small lake, with large lots and only a handful of houses, among them A. D. Russell's. Near the bottom are the Stony Brook public school, a Presbyterian chapel, the old mill site of 1714 and the estate of Jos. S. Bruere along Stony Brook, which is drawn in blue across the lower part of the sheet. The blocks between Springdale Road and Oldens Lane are drawn in a separate inset at the right (part 2). Scale bar and water pipes are shown; most roads are lettered with their widths.
notes: Hazlet Road on the sheet is today's Haslet Avenue; Oldens Lane is Olden Lane; the road lettered Stony Brook is Quaker Road.
Drawn at 200 feet to an inch, north toward the upper left.
The Edgerstoune Road / Stockton Street junction, hand-picked, lies about 13 to 17 m from a fit to the other points and is left out of the fit; the drawn entry may differ from the modern one.

200 ft, north to the upper left. Two parts: 1 main (Stockton St, Elm Rd, Lovers Ln, Mercer St, Oldens Ln = Olden Lane, Battle Rd, Hazlet Rd = Haslet Av, Ober Rd, Edgerstoune, Stony Brook road = Quaker Rd; sparse, hand-picked points), 2 inset (Springdale Rd to Oldens Ln, Hazlet, Ober, Newlin Rds; same scale, a few degrees turned).

sheet-20-2.description: An inset at the right of sheet 20, outlined by a heavy line and drawn at 200 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing the new residential blocks between Springdale Road and Oldens Lane, south of the seminary and west of the university grounds. Hazlet Road runs along the slanted west side of the inset, and Ober Road and Newlin Road cross from Springdale Road to Oldens Lane, dividing the ground into blocks numbered 148 to 152. The houses are mostly frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories on large lots, each lettered with its owner: W. H. Sayer, W. C. Vandewater, H. W. Dodds, C. Besore, G. T. Miner, T. H. Anderson, R. W. Baker, H. E. Bowman, F. S. Cart, M. Hutchison, H. B. Slusser, R. W. Shelton and M. G. Buchanan among them, with a club building on Ober Road. Several lots are still empty. Water pipes run in all the streets, with hydrants at the corners. The inset joins sheet 10 along Hazlet Road and the top of the main map of sheet 20 along Oldens Lane.
notes: Hazlet Road is today's Haslet Avenue; Oldens Lane is Olden Lane.
The inset is turned a few degrees from the main map of the sheet and placed apart from it on the page.

200 ft, north to the upper left. Two parts: 1 main (Stockton St, Elm Rd, Lovers Ln, Mercer St, Oldens Ln = Olden Lane, Battle Rd, Hazlet Rd = Haslet Av, Ober Rd, Edgerstoune, Stony Brook road = Quaker Rd; sparse, hand-picked points), 2 inset (Springdale Rd to Oldens Ln, Hazlet, Ober, Newlin Rds; same scale, a few degrees turned).

sheet-21-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 21 shows a residential district of large suburban estates on the west side of Princeton borough at 100 feet to an inch, below the heavy line that bounds the top strip. Cleveland Lane sweeps in a wide curve from Elm Road at the left to Library Place at the right, Lafayette Road runs diagonally from the northeast to meet Hodge Road at the bottom right, and Hodge Road follows a long curve across the lower half of the sheet. Elm Road and Rosedale Road bound the district on the west, and Library Place runs down the right edge. Westcott Road curves along the upper right edge. The ground is divided into large lots, most of them with a single frame or brick dwelling and outbuildings set well back from the road, among them the H. B. Gardner house at the lower left. Most of the land between the roads is blank, with lot lines but no buildings. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along the streets, and house numbers are lettered along the roads. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at the top near the heavy line, and the margins carry no exposure notes where the sheet ends. The sheet adjoins sheets 79, 83, 84, 85, 102 and 107 and a trolley right of way and borough limit line appear at the upper right.
notes: Cleveland Lane, Lafayette Road, Hodge Road and Library Place on this sheet postdate the 1911 edition. Hodge Road and the Lafayette Road / Hodge Road fork were left out: the drawn Hodge Road is about 20 to 40 percent longer between junctions than the modern one, so it is probably displaced or realigned.
Placed from three hand-picked points, two from pipe crossings and one rough reading at Elm Road; no automatic detections, no independent check. Low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Elm Rd, Cleveland Ln, Lafayette Rd, Hodge Rd; Hodge Road drawn 20 to 40 percent longer than modern, left out; 3 hand-picked points), 2 top strip (Westcott Rd, Bayard Ln; anchored).

sheet-21-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 21 is the strip along the top of the sheet above the heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It shows Westcott Road curving across the strip from the left, with Library Place bending off it at the left, and Bayard Lane running down from the top at the right edge. A row of dwellings with large lots stands along the north side of Westcott Road, with a few outbuildings, and below the road lie narrow deep lots running toward the heavy line. A north arrow stands at the top. Water pipes of six inches are drawn along Westcott Road and Bayard Lane, and house numbers are lettered along Westcott Road. The boundary notes at the top read no exposure, and block numbers 107, 83 and 6 identify the adjoining sheets. The strip is separately framed because it is drawn from a different survey from the main map below it, and it has a single control point.
notes: Anchored on one hand-picked rough point (Bayard Lane / Westcott Road) with the main part's scale and rotation. The Library Place / Westcott Road junction at the left could not be matched to a modern node. Low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main (Elm Rd, Cleveland Ln, Lafayette Rd, Hodge Rd; Hodge Road drawn 20 to 40 percent longer than modern, left out; 3 hand-picked points), 2 top strip (Westcott Rd, Bayard Ln; anchored).
